PullRequest.Title: agentHost: expose root config before AHP authentication

## Summary

Expose full root configuration, including listener-owned project catalogues, to transport-admitted relay clients before AHP authentication.

The root reducer ignores `root/configChanged` when the initial snapshot has no `config`. Omitting it during discovery means clients that authenticate after subscribing cannot populate their project catalogue without an additional root subscription.

- Include configuration in initial, subscribed, and reconnect root snapshots.
- Deliver configuration updates and reconnect replay before authentication and after identity expiry.
- Keep session-content access, non-root subscriptions, configuration writes, passive mutation restrictions, and rejection isolation protected by the existing authorization gates.
- Cover active/passive clients, initially empty/already-loaded catalogues, and reducer application through authentication and reconnect without another subscription.
- Update the Mission Control discovery and authorization documentation.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --reporter dot` — 356 passed, 1 skipped.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts` — passed.
- Signed commit pre-commit hygiene — passed.

The first build attempt encountered an existing installed SDK/runtime version mismatch. `npm run install-fast` restored the declared dependencies, after which the build and checks passed without dependency-manifest changes.

A live mobile-client connection was not tested.

Current-head CI passed: [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39067323282), [Monaco Editor checks](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39067323252), [CodeQL](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39067323257), [Component Fixtures](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39067323258), and [Telemetry](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39067323262). Code OSS exercised Electron, browser, remote, and smoke tests across Linux, macOS, and Windows; unrelated CLI, Copilot, and chat-lib jobs were skipped by change detection.

Copilot reviewed the current head with no open issues. The broader pre-AHP configuration-read surface is intentional; session-content access and mutation authorization remain unchanged.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed predicate, replay loop, 1,000-action bound, full-config projection, clone-progress publisher, and 32 MiB transport ceiling are all directly traced. Exact config sizes and the number of updates missed by a typical mobile disconnect are uncertain, which limits severity, but the multiplicative payload mechanism and reconnect critical-path placement are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serialized full-root-configuration bytes and Web PubSub frames
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Reconnect payload size now grows as O(U × C), where U is the number of root configuration/catalogue updates since the client's last sequence (up to the 1,000-entry replay buffer) and C is the full overlaid root-config size; each retained update is projected as a complete replace action rather than a delta.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased reconnect latency and network/serialization pressure, with sufficiently large histories reaching the 32 MiB single-payload ceiling and closing the lane instead of reconnecting
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this added allowlist case, an unauthenticated reconnect filtered every RootConfigChanged envelope, so its replay response contained no accumulated full-configuration history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Unauthenticated reconnects now retain every RootConfigChanged envelope in the replay range; the reconnect path collects all matching replay-buffer entries, and _projectRelayRootAction replaces each with the full overlaid configuration captured by _relayRootConfigEnvelopes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `envelope.action.type !== ActionType.RootConfigChanged` allowlist term at line 3854 is what changes pre-auth reconnect filtering from zero config envelopes to all matching config envelopes; tests in this diff explicitly change replay expectations from `actions: []` to a config action.
Findings.Title: Coalesce configuration updates before reconnect replay
Findings.Impact: A relay client reconnecting before reauthentication after a long project clone or a series of host-setting/catalogue changes must download and parse every intermediate full configuration before it can make progress. MissionControlProjects publishes catalogue progress repeatedly, and the global replay buffer can retain 1,000 actions, so a sizeable MCP/customization config is duplicated many times in one Web PubSub response.
Findings.Evidence: _restoreReconnectSubscriptions iterates the entire replay buffer and pushes every relevant envelope; this changed predicate makes RootConfigChanged relevant pre-auth. _recordAndBroadcastAction stores every successful config update in _relayRootConfigEnvelopes as `{ config: values, replace: true }`, where `values` is a deep clone of the complete native config plus the extension overlay, and _projectRelayRootAction returns that full envelope. MissionControlProjects._publish emits these actions for clone start/progress/completion. The Mission Control transport serializes the whole reconnect result and chunking rejects payloads above 32 MiB.
Findings.Recommendation: When projecting a pre-auth replay, collapse successful RootConfigChanged envelopes to the latest full `replace: true` envelope (preserving the latest server sequence), or switch to a fresh root snapshot once more than a small bounded amount of config history would be replayed. Intermediate full replacements are not needed to reconstruct the final catalogue/config state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unauthenticated Mission Control initialize or root subscribe receives the host configuration and project catalogue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The in-memory root snapshot is projected, the full config is deep-cloned and overlaid when the Copilot extension is present, then the initialize/subscribe response is JSON-serialized, framed, and published over Web PubSub before discovery completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deep-clone/overlay the root config and JSON-serialize the response into Web PubSub framing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per returned root snapshot; payload work is linear in full config and catalogue size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pre-auth projection omitted config, so it did not clone or serialize those bytes; authenticated snapshots already paid this cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the initialize/subscribe response can be published

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish initialize/subscribe response through the Mission Control Web PubSub lane
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical response, split into approximately payloadBytes/900KiB frames when large
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same response boundary existed, but its pre-auth payload omitted full configuration bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery waits for delivery of the response

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full root-schema/config byte size plus project-catalogue cardinality; one effective root snapshot per initialize or explicit root subscription. Duplicate reconnect subscription URIs are deduplicated, while initialize subscriptions are client supplied.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Projection is synchronous on the protocol handler. Mission Control permits at most 32 lanes; outbound publication is bounded globally to 64 in-flight publishes and 4 MiB, with at most four in-flight chunk frames per lane queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The snapshot reads current in-memory root state and the extension's in-memory project map. Before project initialization the catalogue can be empty; after load it is warm in memory. There is no snapshot/result cache or request coalescing, but this scenario performs one required transfer per handshake/subscription.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: projection, cloning, serialization, framing, and lane limits are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical root-config and project-catalogue sizes are not established; the added work is bounded per handshake and is required to expose the requested state, so it is not independently reportable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. This adds linear required payload work once per discovery response without repeated boundaries or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: A subscribed unauthenticated or expired client receives live host-config and project-catalogue changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A RootConfigChanged action is captured as a complete native-plus-extension replacement, checked against each active lane subscription, serialized per eligible lane, and queued to Web PubSub. The client update waits on that publish, while the underlying clone continues independently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing `git clone --progress` operation emits progress that can cause catalogue publications
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git subprocess per clone; progress events are coalesced by a 1-second ThrottledDelayer
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloning and progress publication already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess is the source of progress but notification publication does not wait for clone completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build one full replacement config envelope, then serialize it for each eligible lane
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full config capture per update and one framed serialization per eligible subscribed lane, up to 32
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unauthenticated/expired lanes were filtered before send; authenticated lanes already received the same action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization occurs synchronously before each update is queued

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the config action to each subscribed Mission Control client group
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical publication per eligible lane per update, with chunking for large configs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No config publication was made to pre-auth or expired lanes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client visibility waits for its lane's queue and acknowledgements; clone work itself remains off this network critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of eligible root-subscribed lanes (maximum 32) times full overlaid config bytes times update frequency. Project clone progress uses a 1-second delayed/coalescing publisher, and settings/catalogue mutations also emit updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Broadcast iterates lanes synchronously. Web PubSub queues per client and drains under global 64-publish/4-MiB in-flight bounds; batching can combine queued small messages for capable clients but does not eliminate duplicated full config per lane.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The complete overlaid config envelope is built once per source action and retained by WeakMap while its replay-buffer key remains live. There is no per-client recomputation of the overlay, but serialization/network transfer occurs per lane. Progress triggers are delayed/coalesced for bursts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed eligibility and per-lane publication are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously pre-auth/expired subscribed lanes and real config sizes are uncertain. Lane, queue, and progress coalescing bounds make live delivery alone a limited expansion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate live-fanout finding. The new recipients are required by the feature, bounded to 32 lanes, and progress bursts are already delayed/coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: A Mission Control client reconnects before reauthentication and requests replay of missed root updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconnect restores the root subscription, scans the bounded replay buffer, retains every now-allowed RootConfigChanged event after the client's sequence, projects each to its captured full replacement config, then serializes the entire actions array into one reconnect response before the client can resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize an actions array containing every missed full replacement configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: U complete config copies in one response, U <= 1,000; bytes scale as U × C
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-auth relevance filter removed all RootConfigChanged actions, so reconnect replay carried zero config-history bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All replay collection and serialization must complete before reconnect can return; payloads above 32 MiB are rejected

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the chunked reconnect response over the client's Web PubSub group
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical response split into O(U × C / 900KiB) acknowledged frames
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same response boundary existed, but config replay did not contribute frames before authentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reconnect completion waits for transfer and client parsing; larger histories consume queue capacity and increase latency

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Missed root-config/catalogue update count U (up to the 1,000-entry replay buffer) times complete overlaid config size C. Subscription URIs are deduplicated, but replayed config actions are not coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replay construction is synchronous after subscription restoration. One reconnect response is serialized/chunked; lane framing permits a maximum 32-MiB application payload and queues chunks under per-lane/global backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The replay buffer is a warm bounded history, not a latest-value cache. Each config envelope has a precomputed full replacement overlay, but all historical replacements are included. If the cursor is older than the buffer or baseline is missing, the code falls back to one current snapshot instead.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed allowlist, replay scan, 1,000-entry bound, full replacement projection, and 32-MiB framing ceiling are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact missed-update counts and host-config sizes vary, so severity is medium rather than high. Long clones, settings changes, authentication-triggered catalogue publications, and temporary mobile disconnects provide realistic multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression. Intermediate full replacement configs are unnecessary to reconstruct the final state and can multiply reconnect payload size until the lane fails.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence reconnect regression was submitted: pre-auth replay now includes every missed full-config replacement instead of coalescing to the latest state. Snapshot and live-update costs were analyzed but are bounded required transfers and were not separately reported.
